To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the EU issue boosted support for the Centre Party and the Socialist Left Party and that (ii) the EU issue attenuated support for the Labour Party and the Progress party.
the EU issue had a negative impact on the support for the governing Labour Party and the Centre Party, but a positive impact on the support of the Conservative Party and the Socialist Left Party.
the EU issue was a significant factor in the Norwegian 1993 parliamentary and 1994 referendum elections and that it was the EU-sceptical parties who gained most from the referendum debate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of voting behaviour in elections and referenda, and the relationship between the two.
the relationship between direct and indirect forms of democracy.
the relationship between the EU referendum and the 1993 general election.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EU issue was of considerable importance to Norwegian voters in the 1990s.
the EU issue did not influence voting in the 1994 referendum in a straightforward manner, but it had some impact on voting in the 2001 referendum.
the referendum outcome was influenced by the 1993 election results, but not the other way around.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the referendum outcome can only be understood in light of the electoral context in which the referendum was held.
EU-scepticism is a strong and persistent force in Norwegian politics.
the 1994 referendum on EU membership was not a mere'referendum on referendums'.
The main takeaway from our work is that
referendums are not isolated from the political system.
the EU issue is not a 'free-rider' issue.
the referendum and election nexus is a complex and multi-faceted phenomenon.
